en: My collarbones were rubbed raw,
And the flesh of my sides was torn.
It became clear that this darkened,
Treacherous world had left me behind.
There is no forest for the blind,
Alive today and gone tomorrow,
And I had no strength left to gird my waist.
When I escaped my suffering,
My valiant uncle was no longer there.
When I lamented, my tongue poured forth,
While my two eyes blazed.
I could do nothing by my own will,
For my two hands were bound.
Brave Kyyaz’s herd of horses,
His surging, gleaming herd!
It thundered down from above,
And tending horses was hell.
For the herdsman himself,
I hurriedly carried firewood.
Unable to face the day of death,
As the day grew late and the sun set,
That herdsman clubbed me
Until my skin was tanned raw.
When dawn broke bright,
I danced like a Kalmyk.
When the sun reached midmorning,
I slung a milk pail around my neck.
The hell of this world—
This is how I endured it.
I carried birch firewood,
While the herdsman drank his fill within.
He made me gnaw clean and swallow
The knucklebones of two horses.
I was imprisoned by a hostile slave,
And beaten by the herdsman.
Saying, “The slave has grown insolent,”
They plundered what little I possessed.
The garden-city of our fortune was bound,
And our destiny was broken then.
Disgraced, my eyes still blazed;
Thus did my misery boil.
I suffered torment from the enemy,
And cruel humiliation crushed my soul.
Only a spoonful of blood remained in me,
My flesh was but a blue, raw scrap.
At that time I thought,
“The death of this wretched head
Has arrived without my dying.”
I thought, “The strength and vigor
Of my steel-boned body are gone.”
Lioness maiden, hear my words:
Many burdens cling to a man at death;
Surging strength and courage
Disappear one day,
In the blink of an eye.
While the vigor of youth remains,
While fortune is in its season,
A man destroys those he pursues,
And when he holds dominion,
He subdues the whole world
And rules over it.
That dear cap of blue lynx fur—
Who has not worn it jauntily?
While luck and fortune remain,
Who has not walked with thunderous pride?
At the name “Brave Külchoro,”
Did the whole age not tremble in fear?
No mortal dared confront me,
No enemy willingly sought me.
At the mere word “enemy” or “foe,”
Blood burst from his flanks,
And life fled at my voice.
The critic who tried me died.
The land grieved without seeing me,
And the spy who grieved the land died.
Such a valiant choro was I,
A lion no pleading enemy could capture,
A warrior upheld by the spirits.
Laughter made the day set,
And merriment made the dawn break.
Both merry and lionhearted,
Both champion and hero—
Such a choro was I.
I was a glowing ember of red steel,
I too was an arrow
Shot forth from the Kyrgyz.
But now I have fallen into ruin;
When I reflect, no strength remains in my limbs.
I am no longer myself.
Again exhausted and gaunt,
I have grown thin.
My powers spent and strength gone,
I have grown old.
In the days when fortune was mine,
When true battle-fury seized me,
We wrought slaughter among the Oirats.
When we charged in wrath,
We raided and conquered the Chinese.
When the fever of battle came upon us,
We wrought utter ruin.
When we charged and poured forth our rage,
We slaughtered every last enemy.
Now my final reckoning has come,
And heroic courage, strength, and vigor
Have been struck from me and gone.
The reason I have been brought so low
Is that yesterday Sarybai, son of a monster,
Unleashed all his power,
Piling up torment mountain-high.
Roaring like a hungry lion,
He overran the plain and cleared a path,
Invaded and plundered Talas,
Seizing all the spoils,
And wreaking terrible destruction.
My courage surged and my heart burned.
If true death comes, I shall die;
If God truly wills it,
If true death comes, I shall die.
My words spoken early came too late,
And I watched with desperate longing.
My eyes flared with indignation,
And, still alive, my heart boiled.
Against that infidel, the monster’s son,
I stood first on one bank, then the other.
Shooting hard and drawing my bow,
I fought him in a bloody clash.
I lacked the strength to strike him down,
And could not defeat the vicious dog.
My stout ribs came apart,
And my frailty was revealed.
Tears poured from my eyes,
And both my spears shattered.
The tears flowing from both eyes
Fell upon my chest.
Twelve steel and a thousand spears
Were shattered in the jousting.
Twelve chargers and countless swift horses
Were killed and lay fallen in combat.
Thus my strength proved insufficient.
It seems I have fallen into ruin.
I have none of my former strength;
It seems I am no longer myself.
Our sorrows gathered and overwhelmed us,
And our honor faded away.
You are the strength with which we gird our waists,
Our lioness maiden,
The warrior who brings us blessing.
Grim-featured is Sarybai,
A fearsome enemy such as this.
My charger’s back has grown sore from riding,
And my heart ached from fighting.
My noble steed grew weary,
And my noble head was hard-pressed.
Maiden champion, lioness,
We look to you as our protector.
Should the boastful infidel
Stir up some fresh conflict,
May you deliver the lionhearted warrior
And save him from suffering—
Such is my desire.
For many years before you came,
Against that fiend of surpassing cruelty,
When I thrust willingly, my spear would not pierce;
When I grappled, my strength fell short;
When I struck, my axe would not bite;
When I fired my white musket, its bullet would not pierce.
All the valiant men were destroyed,
And the world cried out that I was dead.
He prolonged the great turmoil,
Dragging maidens away as plunder,
Robbing me of much of my former self,
And thus battering my spirit.
He raided and humiliated us,
And seized my peaceful possessions by force.
When I wrestled him, my strength fell short;
When I struck true, my hand could not penetrate.
Against this infidel Sarybai,
This swaggering warrior,
Khans with sound arms died,
And every soul who grappled with him died.
My surging rage boiled,
But my strength fell short against the hellion;
Thus did my misery boil.”
So spoke Külchoro,
His exhaustion plain to see.
Unable to overcome Sarybai,
Külchoro despaired of life.
As Külchoro stood there,
Speaking softly and casting forth her fortune,
Kuyaly began to speak:
“This is the armor the monster’s infidel son
Wears when he enters combat;
This is the arm with which he wrestles;
That is the man who boasts himself a hero.
I have driven men down and crushed them into disgrace;
I am that wretched warrior.
His origin is alien and his venom strong;
Let us reach that doomed slave
And perish together with him.
I shall settle the proper reckoning;
If he fights, I shall find a way.
If the villain proves obstinate,
We shall gouge out his eyes.
If the villain grows enraged,
We shall lay him out full-length.
Thus shall we take revenge;
If the villain strains against us,
We shall settle his true account.”
She summoned her courage and made ready,
And in place of her former stratagem,
Inspiration came to her from the unseen.
She arranged all her battle gear,
And bloodthirsty Zulpukor
Was fastened bare at her waist.
Without speaking a word,
She growled and worked herself into fury,
Threatening Sarybai.
She thrust out her chest like a hungry lion,
Her eyes wide as an open grave.
The blood drained from her face,
And the sight of her distracted the mind.
If you observed the fierce-eyed maiden,
When she surges against that maiden,
No mortal can stand before her.
Not Sarybai—the whole wide world
Could not confront and defeat her.
With a crest like a fleeing kulan,
A gold-browed, high-arched saddle,
Was fitted upon Zhelzhetpes, swift as the wind,
Like a sovereign ruling a people.
Prancing proudly, Zhelzhetpes
Seemed destined for good fortune.
He champed upon his bit,
And tore the ground wherever he stepped.
The black earth struck by his hooves
Split apart on every side.
His banner-like tail was a piled-up mass,
Revealing the form of a noble steed.
When he strode with bounding steps, the black earth
Scattered like fragments of a great bowl.
A great falcon broad as a house
Shrieked above her head.
She made her charger rear and plunge,
Throwing all the people into an uproar.
“The maiden is a lion!” they said,
Delighting everyone who saw her.
An ancestral spirit descended upon the maiden;
The tasseled banners parted amid the host.
Her majestic presence,
Her bearing upon horseback,
Loomed like a towering mountain.
Every mortal being’s
Wits were utterly confounded.
She looked to either side,
Licking her lips like a hungry lion.
